title: Cloud Resource Tag Compliance and Drift

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.15 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.15 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:config:resource` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Resource Graph, GCP Asset Inventory; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Resource Graph, GCP Asset Inventory
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:resource" tag_compliance="non_compliant"
| table _time resourceType resourceId awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.15_cloud_resource_tag_compl_15"
| sort -_time
description: Missing or inconsistent tags (Owner, CostCenter, Environment) block cost allocation, automation, and governance. Detecting untagged or non-compliant resources supports tag policy enforcement.
value: Detecting cloud resource tag compliance and drift early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Use AWS Config rules (required-tags), Azure Policy (e.g. RequireTagAndValue), or GCP org policy for label requirements. Ingest compliance results. Alert when net new untagged resources appear or compliance score drops below threshold. Dashboard by OU/account and resource type.
visualization: Table (account, resource type, non-compliant count), Gauge (tag compliance %), Bar chart by tag key missing.
knownFalsePositives: A plan can show a diff right after a release while state catches up, or when we intentionally tuned something in the console during an emergency. We confirm the workspace and the window before we treat it as unplanned drift.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Resource Graph, GCP Asset Inventory with the modular input for `aws:config:resource`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `resourceType` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Use AWS Config rules (required-tags), Azure Policy (e.g. RequireTagAndValue), or GCP org policy for label requirements. Ingest compliance results. Alert when net new untagged resources appear or compliance score drops below threshold. Dashboard by OU/account and resource type.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:resource" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:resource" tag_compliance="non_compliant"
| table _time resourceType resourceId awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.15_cloud_resource_tag_compl_15"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:config:resource` in `index=aws` to detect cloud resource tag compliance and drift. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `resourceType` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_15_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Table (account, resource type, non-compliant count), Gauge (tag compliance %), Bar chart by tag key missing..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Resource Graph, GCP Asset Inventory and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cloud resource tag compliance and drift so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
